mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 2.0% compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporate investment.
failure_condition: SPX 20d forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0% (25th percentile of historical values).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 3.0% signals active monetary tightening, increasing real borrowing costs and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate broad demand contraction, triggering earnings revisions downward and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS < 650,000 and HOUST < 1500, SPX 20d forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 3.5%), rising employment (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 3.5%, PAYEMS growth fails to produce positive 5d returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production (INDPRO > 105) indicates robust manufacturing output, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 105 fails to predict positive 60d returns in more than 60% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Consumer price inflation exceeding 5.0% (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%) triggers central bank tightening expectations, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rises in inflation (CPIAUCSL > 0.5% MoM) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 0.25% MoM) signal aggressive monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises >0.5% and FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% in the same month, SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In high GDP growth regimes (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized), strong industrial production (INDPRO > 105) indicates sustained manufacturing output, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In periods where GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized, INDPRO > 105 fails to produce positive 60d returns in more than 60% of cases.
